mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has declined steadily for three consecutive weeks (-1.9 to -10.7), reflecting reduced commuting and associated weekday errands and lunchtime shopping trips. This sustained workplace contraction directly suppresses nearby retail and recreation footfall, so RETAIL_REC should continue trending lower over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -1.9 to -10.7 over three weeks
failure_condition: Hypothesis is rejected if mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days rises above the last-28-day mean despite WORKPLACES continuing to decline or staying flat below -10.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility falls below -12 percent, this signals an escalation to stricter distancing or work-from-home mandates, which typically coincide with tighter limits on retail operating capacity or hours, driving RETAIL_REC down within two weeks of the crossing.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -12 percent from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES at t-0w is -10.7 and accelerating downward
failure_condition: Hypothesis fails if WORKPLACES crosses below -12 but RETAIL_REC does not fall or instead rises over the following two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Rising RESIDENTIAL time (8.7 to 9.1) combined with persistently depressed TRANSIT (-15.0 to -15.7) indicates households are both staying home more and avoiding transit-dependent trips. The joint effect of reduced mobility range and increased home-centric behavior compounds to suppress discretionary retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks beyond what either series alone would predict.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose each week while TRANSIT stayed near -15
failure_condition: Hypothesis fails if RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated and TRANSIT remains depressed, indicating no compounding suppression effect.

mechanism_narrative: The co-movement of falling WORKPLACES and rising RESIDENTIAL over three consecutive weeks is characteristic of an active tightening-restriction regime. In this regime, retail and recreation venues face capacity or hour restrictions that lag announcement by about a week, so RETAIL_REC should keep falling through the next four weeks as long as this regime persists.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES down and RESIDENTIAL up simultaneously across snapshot
failure_condition: Hypothesis fails if WORKPLACES stabilizes or reverses upward (indicating regime exit) yet RETAIL_REC continues to decline, or if RETAIL_REC rises while the tightening regime signals persist.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has recovered sharply from -18.3 to -11.0 over three weeks, the strongest rebound among all categories. Since parks and retail/recreation both represent discretionary leisure activity, this recovery signals rising willingness to leave home for leisure, which should feed through to a short-term uptick in RETAIL_REC within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -18.3 to -11.0 over three weeks
failure_condition: Hypothesis fails if PARKS continues improving next week but RETAIL_REC's weekly mean does not rise or falls further.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility drops more than 3 points week-on-week from its current -15.7 level, this would indicate a new behavioral shift toward avoiding public transit, likely reflecting fear of exposure or new restrictions, which would cut off a key access route to retail and recreation destinations within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 3 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has been flat near -15 to -15.7 for three weeks
failure_condition: Hypothesis fails if TRANSIT drops by more than 3 points in a week but RETAIL_REC does not decline over the subsequent two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has stayed within a narrow band (-1.1 to -4.1) without a clear trend, suggesting routine, non-panic shopping behavior consistent with a seasonally stable period. This stability signals an underlying steady-state consumer routine that should allow RETAIL_REC to gradually normalize upward over the next four weeks as discretionary spending resumes alongside stable essential-shopping patterns.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fluctuates narrowly between -1.1 and -4.1 across four weeks
failure_condition: Hypothesis fails if GROCERY_PHARM remains stable yet RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean falls below its prior-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous decline of WORKPLACES (-1.9 to -10.7) and persistently low TRANSIT (around -15) jointly indicate that commuting-linked retail spillover, which depends on both workplace presence and transit-enabled trip chaining, is collapsing faster than either series alone would suggest. This compounded loss of trip-chaining opportunity should depress RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES declining while TRANSIT remains near -15 throughout snapshot
failure_condition: Hypothesis fails if both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain depressed or worsen together but RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next two weeks.
